meta.title: From scratch, every morning: the quiet arithmetic of a small-town bakery
meta.deck: Unit test 1. A family bakery in an ageing Japanese town, told with 73 expressions from the first three articles.
meta.note: 第 1 单元测试：用前三篇学过的 73 个表达写成的新文章。建议先关掉“标出生词”和“显示译文”，看自己能读懂多少，再对照讲解。这里的生词和原文章共用复习进度。这是一篇原创练习文章，人物和店铺是虚构的。

sents.en: From scratch, every morning: the quiet arithmetic of a small-town bakery
sents.zh: 每天清晨从头做起：一家小镇面包店的精打细算
notes: from scratch：从零开始、用原材料自己做。面包店每天从面粉开始做面包，字面意思和引申义都说得通。
arithmetic：算术，这里指经营上要算的账。the quiet arithmetic = 不声不响的精打细算。

sents.en: In an ageing town where shops sit empty, one family bakery has survived for 60 years.
sents.zh: 在一个老龄化、店铺纷纷空置的小镇上，一家家庭面包店已经撑了六十年。
notes: where 引导定语从句，修饰 town。
sit empty：空着、闲置。
has survived for 60 years：现在完成时加 for，表示从过去一直持续到现在。

sents.en: How long it can keep going is another story.
sents.zh: 它还能撑多久，就是另一回事了。
notes: How long it can keep going 是名词性从句作主语，所以用陈述语序 it can，不是 can it。
X is another story：X 则另当别论、X 是另一回事。

sents.en: Most mornings, Kenji Sato is at work by four, long before the first commuters slump onto the early train.
sents.zh: 大多数早上，佐藤健二四点前就开工了，比第一批通勤的人瘫坐上早班车要早得多。
notes: by four：四点之前。by + 时间 = 不晚于某个时间。
long before：早在……之前很久。
slump onto：瘫坐到……上，写出通勤者没睡醒的样子。

sents.en: He makes everything from flour, butter and patience, and he is in no hurry to change.
sents.zh: 他用面粉、黄油和耐心做出所有东西，也一点都不急着改变。
notes: flour, butter and patience：前两样是真材料，第三样是比喻，并列在一起有点幽默。
be in no hurry to do sth：一点也不急着做某事。

sents.en: His grandfather opened the shop in 1964, and the oven, the scales and the wooden till have stayed where they were ever since.
sents.zh: 他祖父 1964 年开了这家店，烤炉、秤和木头收银台从那以后就一直放在原处。
notes: scales：秤，这个意思常用复数。
till：收银台（英式）。
have stayed ... ever since：现在完成时配 ever since，“从那以后一直……”。

sents.en: Walking in feels like stepping into a time capsule.
sents.zh: 走进店里，就像走进了一个时间胶囊。
notes: Walking in 是动名词作主语。feel like + 动名词：感觉像在做某事。
time capsule：时间胶囊，比喻一切都停留在过去的地方。

sents.en: On Saturdays customers queue out of the door, and a surprising number of them are young people from the city with nowhere to be.
sents.zh: 每到周六，顾客一直排到门外，其中年轻人多得让人意外，都是从城里来、没什么急事要赶的人。
notes: queue out of the door：队伍排到门外。queue 作动词是英式用法。
a surprising number of：数量多得让人意外，后接复数名词。
with nowhere to be：没有要赶去的地方，也就是不赶时间。

sents.en: The bakery is famously cash-only.
sents.zh: 这家面包店只收现金，这一点出了名。
notes: famously：出了名地。
cash-only：只收现金，用连字符连成一个形容词。

sents.en: Its prices are gloriously dull: a loaf has cost the same for a decade.
sents.zh: 它的价格乏味得可爱：一条面包十年都没涨过价。
notes: gloriously dull：乏味得可爱。用褒义的 gloriously 修饰贬义的 dull，是带着欣赏的反话。
冒号后面具体解释“乏味”指什么：价格十年不变。

sents.en: Regulars count out coins at the counter, while visitors fumble for their wallets and look around for a card reader that is not there.
sents.zh: 老顾客在柜台前一枚一枚数硬币，外地来的人则手忙脚乱地找钱包，还四处找根本没有的刷卡机。
notes: regulars：常客、老顾客。
count out：一个一个地数出来。
fumble for：笨手笨脚地摸找。
while 连接对比的两组人：老顾客从容，外地人慌乱。

sents.en: Mr Sato sees it differently from his younger customers: card firms take a slice of every sale, and he already lives on thin margins.
sents.zh: 佐藤先生和年轻顾客看法不同：信用卡公司每笔交易都要抽走一块，而他本来利润就很薄。
notes: see it differently：看法不同。
a slice of：……的一部分（像切下的一片）。
thin margins：利润微薄。live on thin margins = 靠很薄的利润过日子。

sents.en: Cash, he argues, is not broken, so there is no reason to fix it.
sents.zh: 他说，现金又没坏，没理由去修它。
notes: he argues 是插入语。
化用了俗语 If it ain't broke, don't fix it（没坏就别修），意思是没有问题就不必改。

sents.en: Counterintuitively, refusing cards may even save him money.
sents.zh: 和直觉相反，不收卡反而可能让他省钱。
notes: counterintuitively：与直觉相反地，放在句首修饰整句。
refusing cards 是动名词作主语。save sb money = 给某人省钱。

sents.en: Whereas a card payment costs him a fee, a coin dropped into the till costs him nothing extra.
sents.zh: 刷卡付款要付他一笔手续费，而一枚丢进收银台的硬币不会让他多花一分钱。
notes: whereas：而、然而，用来对比两件事。
dropped into the till 是过去分词短语，修饰 a coin。
nothing extra：没有额外的。形容词放在 nothing 后面。

sents.en: The real strain on the business is not money but people.
sents.zh: 这门生意真正的压力不在钱，而在人。
notes: the strain on sth：……承受的压力。
not A but B：不是 A 而是 B。

sents.en: Like the rest of Japan, the town's working-age population is shrinking.
sents.zh: 和日本其他地方一样，镇上的劳动年龄人口在减少。
notes: Like the rest of Japan：和日本其他地方一样。
working-age population：劳动年龄人口；shrink：缩小、减少。

sents.en: Bakers willing to start at four in the morning have grown scarce, and the job is among the first to go unfilled.
sents.zh: 愿意凌晨四点开工的面包师已经越来越少，这份工作是最先招不到人的那一批。
notes: willing to start at four in the morning 是形容词短语后置，修饰 bakers。
grow scarce：变得稀缺，这里用现在完成时 have grown scarce。
among the first to do sth：最早……的那一批之一。go unfilled：空着没人填。

sents.en: For weeks on end last winter, Mr Sato and his wife covered the gaps themselves, working almost around the clock.
sents.zh: 去年冬天，佐藤夫妇一连好几周自己顶上空缺，几乎是昼夜不停地干。
notes: for weeks on end：一连好几周。
cover the gaps：填补空缺。
working almost around the clock 是伴随状语，说明他们怎么填补空缺。

sents.en: His son, who has long lived in Osaka, has grudgingly offered to help at weekends.
sents.zh: 他儿子早就住在大阪，勉勉强强地答应周末来帮忙。
notes: have long + 过去分词：早就……、很久以来一直……。has long lived in Osaka = 在大阪住了很久。
grudgingly：不情愿地、勉强地。
at weekends 是英式说法，美式说 on weekends。

sents.en: Mr Sato does not take that for granted.
sents.zh: 佐藤先生并不觉得这是理所当然的。
notes: take sth for granted：把……视为理所当然。that 指儿子来帮忙这件事。

sents.en: A consultant from the city once tried to coax him into opening a second shop, with a card reader, self-checkout and a website.
sents.zh: 城里来的一位顾问曾经想劝他开第二家店，装刷卡机、自助收银，再做个网站。
notes: coax sb into doing sth：好言好语地哄劝某人做某事。
with a card reader, self-checkout and a website 说明这家新店的样子。

sents.en: The incentive was clear: more customers and a hefty share of the tourist trade.
sents.zh: 好处很明显：更多顾客，还能分到游客生意的一大块。
notes: incentive：激励、诱因，让人愿意去做某事的好处。
a hefty share of：相当大的一部分。
冒号后面解释 incentive 具体是什么。

sents.en: Mr Sato listened politely, handed over a free loaf, and said no.
sents.zh: 佐藤先生礼貌地听完，递上一条免费的面包，然后拒绝了。
notes: 三个动词并列：listened, handed over, said，节奏很快，写出他拒绝得干脆。
hand over：交给、递过去。

sents.en: His reasoning was more rational than it looked.
sents.zh: 他的理由比看上去更合理。
notes: rational：理性的、合乎道理的。
more rational than it looked：it 指 his reasoning，句尾省略了 rational。

sents.en: A bigger business would rest on borrowed money and leave little room for error; a small one can live with a bad month.
sents.zh: 规模大一些的生意要靠借来的钱撑着，几乎容不得出错；小店则扛得住一个不好的月份。
notes: 分号连接两个对比的分句：大生意怎样，小生意怎样。
rest on：建立在……之上。room for error：出错的余地。
live with：忍受、接受（不好的情况）。a small one 的 one 代替 business。

sents.en: Every shortcut, he believes, would chip away at what made the shop indispensable in the first place.
sents.zh: 他认为，每一种省事的办法，都会一点点削弱这家店当初让人离不开的东西。
notes: he believes 是插入语。
chip away at：一点点削弱。
what made the shop indispensable 是名词性从句，作 at 的宾语。in the first place：当初、原本。

sents.en: Over the decades, the bakery has grown into something like a public utility.
sents.zh: 几十年下来，这家面包店已经成了一种近乎公共设施的存在。
notes: over the decades：几十年来。
grow into：发展成。public utility：公用事业，比喻人人离不开。

sents.en: The town has come to count on it, largely because it is always open.
sents.zh: 镇上的人渐渐依赖上了它，主要是因为它总是开着门。
notes: come to do sth：渐渐变得……。
count on：依靠、指望。
largely：主要地、在很大程度上。

sents.en: Neighbours leave parcels there for each other to collect, and anyone who finds a lost possession hands it in at the counter.
sents.zh: 邻居们把包裹放在店里，让彼此来取；谁捡到别人丢的东西，也会交到柜台。
notes: for each other to collect：不定式的逻辑主语用 for 引出，意思是“让彼此来取”。
possession：所有物、个人物品，常用复数 possessions。
hand sth in：上交。宾语是代词时要放中间：hand it in。

sents.en: Reportedly, the shop has returned more lost wallets than the local police box.
sents.zh: 据说，这家店归还的失物钱包比当地的派出所还多。
notes: reportedly：据说、据报道，放在句首表示消息来源不是作者本人。
police box：日本的派出所（交番），上一单元的第一篇讲过。

sents.en: In practice, it works as a small civic centre.
sents.zh: 实际上，它起着一个小型社区中心的作用。
notes: in practice：实际上（与 in theory 相对）。
civic：市民的、公共的。civic centre：社区中心、市民活动中心。centre 是英式拼写。

sents.en: Its virtue lies in the people who stop by, not merely in what they buy.
sents.zh: 它的好处在于来店里的人，而不仅仅在于他们买了什么。
notes: virtue：优点、长处。
lie in：在于。两个 in 短语并列：lies in the people ... not merely in what they buy。
stop by：顺便来一下。not merely：不仅仅。

sents.en: No amount of clever marketing will replace that.
sents.zh: 再高明的营销也代替不了这一点。
notes: no amount of ... will ...：再多的……也不会……。
that 指上一句说的“来店里的人”。

sents.en: Still, rising costs may soon tip the balance.
sents.zh: 不过，不断上涨的成本可能很快就会打破平衡。
notes: still 放句首是“不过、尽管如此”，表示转折。
tip the balance：打破平衡、起决定作用。

sents.en: Flour and electricity prices have crept upward for three years, and the savings that propped up the shop through bad times are running out.
sents.zh: 面粉和电费三年来一直在慢慢上涨，而在困难时期撑住这家店的积蓄也快用完了。
notes: creep upward：慢慢往上涨，crept 是 creep 的过去分词。
prop up：撑住。that propped up the shop through bad times 是定语从句，修饰 savings。
run out：用完、耗尽，进行时表示快用完了。

sents.en: Sooner or later, Mr Sato will have to decide whether the bakery stands to gain more from changing than from staying the same.
sents.zh: 迟早，佐藤先生得想清楚：对面包店来说，改变和不变，哪个更有好处。
notes: sooner or later：迟早。
stand to gain：有望得到好处。
more from changing than from staying the same：比较两种做法带来的好处。

sents.en: For now, he would rather stick with what he knows than give way.
sents.zh: 眼下，他宁可守着自己熟悉的那一套，也不愿让步。
notes: would rather A than B：宁愿 A 也不愿 B，A、B 都用动词原形。
stick with：坚持用、不换掉。give way：让步、屈服。

sents.en: By the time the shop closes each afternoon, almost nothing has gone to waste.
sents.zh: 每天下午关门的时候，几乎没有东西被浪费掉。
notes: by the time ...：到……的时候，主句常用完成时：has gone to waste。
go to waste：被浪费。gone 是过去分词。

sents.en: It is, in its own way, a lesson that travels.
sents.zh: 从它自己的角度看，这是一个到别处也适用的道理。
notes: in its own way：以它自己的方式。
a lesson that travels：能“旅行”的道理，也就是放到别的地方也适用的经验。

cloze.hint: 多得出人意料（a ___ number of）

breakdown.en: A bigger business would rest on borrowed money and leave little room for error; a small one can live with a bad month.
points: 分号把句子分成两半，前后对比：大生意 would ...，小生意 can ...。
前半句是虚拟语气 would：如果他把店做大，就会怎样。主语 A bigger business 后面有两个并列谓语：would rest on ... and leave ...。
rest on borrowed money：要靠借来的钱撑着；leave little room for error：几乎不能出错。
后半句 a small one 的 one 代替 business；live with a bad month = 扛得住一个不好的月份，用的是 can，表示现实中做得到。
